topic: Queued jobs when the with block ends
answer: Leaving the with block waits for the jobs that are already running but cancels the ones still queued, so wait for your results inside the block.

keywords: what happens if the job fails
answer: If the job raised, result() raises relay.JobFailed, and the job's own exception is in .cause. A cancelled job raises relay.Cancelled.
Jobs with the same key run one at a time, in the order you submitted them. Different keys, or no key, run in parallel up to the worker count. runner.limit(key, n) allows n at once.
gather returns outcomes in the order the jobs finished, not the order you passed them. Each outcome has its handle, so keep a dict from handle to whatever the job was for.
outcome.error is the job's exception as it was raised, not wrapped in JobFailed, or a relay.Cancelled if the job was cancelled.
Retry(times=n) runs the job up to n more times after the first, so times=2 means three tries in all. Only exceptions listed in on are retried, and each try starts the function over.
relay can't interrupt a running thread. cancel() and gather's timeout ask the job to stop: relay.cancelled() turns True inside it, and the job should check it between steps and raise relay.Cancelled.
on_finish callbacks run on the thread that finished the job, usually a worker, so several can run at once. Use a lock or relay.Tally for anything they share.
Threads. The jobs here spend their time waiting on the network, so threads are fine.
Anything other than a dropped connection or an offline hospital is a bug, in their data or in our code. Let it fail the sync loudly so someone looks at it.
Don't change relay: other deployments use it. Work around it in supplysync.
Keep pull_all's name and its first two parameters, and keep returning a Pull. Each part says what it adds.
Each hospital's system takes one request at a time; a second one in flight fails with TooManyRequests. Across hospitals, the VPN takes at most four requests at once.
Pages can be fetched in any order, but you only learn how many there are from a page. Page 0 always exists.
Never report part of a hospital's inventory. A hospital is either all there, missing, or late.
The supply team reads it at 6am and reorders anything below par. A missing hospital means they phone that hospital, so it matters that missing is right.
